rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: A report in al-Khiṣāl says God created twelve thousand worlds, each larger than the seven heavens and earths, with each world unaware of the others.
rows.anchor: وفي الخصال عن الصادق عليه السلام قال إن الله تعالى خلق اثنا عشر ألف عالم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report says seven worlds inhabited earth successively before Adam; their inhabitants were not Adam's descendants and were made from earth's surface.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام لقد خلق الله عز وجل في الأرض منذ خلقها سبعة عالمين ليس هم من ولد آدم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عن أبيه عن آبائه عن رسول الله
rows.claim: In response to the claim that Eve came from Adam's rib, the Prophet says God formed Adam from clay and formed Eve from the remaining clay.
rows.anchor: إن الله تبارك وتعالى قبض قبضة من طين فخلطها بيمينه - وكلتا يديه يمين - فخلق منها آدم وفضلت فضلة من الطين فخلق منها حواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports and Genesis say Eve came from Adam's shortest left rib; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this is not impossible in itself, but the Qur'an gives no evidence for it.
rows.anchor: وهناك روايات أخر تدل على أنها خلقت من خلف آدم وهو أقصر أضلاعه من الجانب الأيسر

rows.speaker: السجاد
rows.claim: In a debate, al-Sajjād says Cain married Abel's sister and Abel married Cain's sister; the Quraysh interlocutor asks whether this was their offspring.
rows.anchor: عن السجاد عليه السلام في حديث له مع قرشي يصف فيه تزويج هابيل بلوزا أخت قابيل

rows.speaker: السجاد
rows.claim: Al-Sajjād answers that Magians only practiced sibling marriage after God prohibited it, while it had been an earlier divine law for Adam's family.
rows.anchor: إن المجوس فعلوا ذلك بعد التحريم من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that Adam's wife was created from him and permitted to him accords with the Qur'an's apparent meaning and reason; other reports say the siblings married houris or jinn.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ورد في الحديث هو الموافق لظاهر الكتاب والاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes reports that Cain and Abel married women sent down from houris and jinn, but says his earlier discussion established the correct account.
rows.anchor: وهناك روايات أخر تعارضها وهي تدل على أنهم تزوجوا بمن نزل إليهم من الحور والجان

rows.speaker: الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir interprets the command concerning kinship as an instruction not to sever family ties; the author says this rests on reading the word in the accusative.
rows.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading underlies al-Bāqir's interpretation of the verse's kinship phrase.
rows.anchor: أقول وبناؤه على قراءة النصب

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Kāfī and al-ʿAyyāshī report that God commanded people to maintain human kinship ties and magnified them by pairing them with Himself.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي وتفسير العياشي هي أرحام الناس إن الله عز وجل أمر بصلتها وعظمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's statement that God set kinship alongside Himself refers to their conjunction in the verse's wording.
rows.anchor: والمراد بجعلها معه الاقتران الواقع في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās quoting the Prophet says maintaining kinship makes life last longer in this world and brings good in the next.
rows.anchor:
قال ابن عباس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
" يقول الله تعالى صلوا أرحامكم فإنه أبقى لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī links the report to widely transmitted accounts that kinship ties extend life and severing them has the opposite effect.
rows.anchor: أن صلة الرحم تزيد في العمر وقطعها بالعكس من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests the promise may be supported by the coming discussion of fear for vulnerable descendants left behind.
rows.anchor: بما سيأتي في تفسير قوله تعالى وليخش الذين لو تركوا من خلفهم ذرية ضعافا خافوا عليهم النساء 9 الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, kinship may make life more enduring through its practical effects: family solidarity strengthens people against calamities, enemies, and threats to well-being.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد بكونه أبقى كون الصلة أبقى للحياة من حيث أثرها

rows.speaker: علي عن الأصبغ بن نباتة
rows.claim: ʿAlī says an angry person should approach an angry relative, since contact between kin calms the bond; kinship also appeals to God for those who maintain or sever it.
rows.anchor: سمعت أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام يقول إن أحدكم ليغضب فما يرضى حتى يدخل النار فأيما رجل منكم غضب على ذي رحمه فليدن منه

rows.speaker: علي عن الأصبغ بن نباتة
rows.claim: The report depicts kinship as attached to the Throne, making a metallic ringing sound, and praying for connection or severance according to how people treat it.
rows.anchor: وإنها متعلقة بالعرش تنقضه انتقاض الحديد فتنادي اللهم صل من وصلني واقطع من قطعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship is a real bond of shared descent through one or both parents, with genuine moral, spiritual, bodily, and innate effects that can be weakened but never erased.
rows.anchor: والرحم كما عرفت هي جهة الوحدة الموجودة بين أشخاص الإنسان من حيث اتصال مادة وجودهم في الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because kinship is among the strongest natural bonds, kindness among relatives has greater effect than kindness among strangers, and injury to relatives likewise wounds more deeply.
rows.anchor: فالرحم من أقوى أسباب الالتئام الطبيعي بين أفراد العشيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Approaching a relative honors and strengthens kinship, renewing its effects through compassion and affection.
rows.anchor: فإن الدنو من ذي الرحم رعاية لحكمها وتقوية لجانبها

rows.speaker: الصادق عن أبيه
rows.claim: A report says an angry person should change posture: stand if seated, sit if standing, and approach and touch an angry relative so kinship can calm the anger.
rows.anchor: الصادق عن أبيه عليهما السلام أنه ذكر الغضب فقال إن الرجل ليغضب حتى ما يرضى أبدا ويدخل بذلك النار فأيما رجل غضب وهو قائم فليجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing from standing to sitting redirects attention from impulsive anger and satanic distraction to a new matter; human nature is more inclined toward mercy than anger.
rows.anchor: وفي تغيير الحال من القيام إلى القعود صرف النفس عن شأن إلى شأن جديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the effect of drawing near to kin and touching them is observable and tested.
rows.anchor: أقول وتأثيره محسوس مجرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines inqāḍ as a small sound like tapping; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the Throne will be explained as the station of comprehensive active knowledge of events.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح الإنقاض صويت مثل النقر وقد تقدم في الكلام على الكرسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Throne is the level where scattered events, causes, and cosmic chains converge and from which they are set in motion, like a king's throne directing a kingdom.
rows.anchor: المراد بالعرش مقام العلم الإجمالي الفعلي بالحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship is like a spirit flowing through the forms of people joined by family relation; when oppressed, it seeks refuge in the Throne and asks for help.
rows.anchor: والرحم كما عرفت حقيقة هي كالروح السالب في قوالب الأشخاص الذين يجمعهم جامع القرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image compares the kinship bond's plea to tapping iron, whose resonance and vibration spread throughout its mass, as with bells and metal bowls.
rows.anchor: شبه فيه ما يحدث في هذا الحال بالنقر الواقع على الحديد الذي يحدث فيه رنينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer for those who maintain or sever kinship conveys the substance of its appeal; many reports say maintaining ties lengthens life and cutting them shortens it.
rows.anchor: حكاية لفحوى التجائها واستنصارها وفي الروايات الكثيرة أن صلة الرحم تزيد في العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmic order is directed toward good ends and repairs defective parts or removes them; severing kinship resists this order and, if unreformed, brings shortened life and descendants' extinction.
rows.anchor: وقاطع الرحم يحارب الله في تكوينه فإن لم يصلح بالاستصلاح بتر الله عمره وقطع دابره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may fail to sense this reality because chronic ailments have surrounded human life and dulled its capacity to perceive pain and punishment.
rows.anchor: لأن الأدواء قد أحاطت بجثمان الإنسانية فاختلطت وتشابهت وأزمنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse begins the seven prohibitions arising through marriage or nursing; six appear here and the seventh is stated in the preceding prohibition of fathers' wives.
rows.anchor: شروع في بيان المحرمات بالسبب وهي سبع ست منها ما في هذه الآية وسابعتها ما يتضمنه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse treats nursing as creating legal maternal, filial, and sibling relations, a status al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says is distinctive to Islamic law.
rows.anchor: والآية بسياقها تدل على جعل الأمومة والبنوة بين المرأة ومن أرضعته

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet, in a report accepted by both major traditions, states that nursing prohibits the same relations as lineage, extending prohibition to seven corresponding categories.
rows.anchor: إن الله حرم من الرضاعة ما حرم من النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditions determining when nursing creates prohibition, including amount, manner, and duration, belong to jurisprudence and fall outside this commentary's scope.
rows.anchor: وأما ما به يتحقق الرضاع وما له في نشره الحرمة من الشرائط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A milk sister is a girl whom the man's mother nursed with milk belonging to his father.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به الأخوات الملحقة بالرجل من جهة إرضاع أمه إياها بلبن أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wife's mother is prohibited whether or not the husband consummated the marriage, because wives in this construction means spouses generally, as the later explicit qualification confirms.
rows.anchor: سواء كانت النساء أي الأزواج مدخولا بهن أو غير مدخول بهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stepdaughter is a wife's daughter by another man; she is usually raised by the husband and usually lives in his home, though neither circumstance always applies.
rows.anchor: الربائب جمع الربيبة وهي بنت زوجة الرجل من غيره لأن تدبير أمر من مع المرأة من الولد إلى زوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'in your care' describes the usual situation and does not restrict the prohibition; a stepdaughter remains prohibited even when she did not live in her stepfather's home.
rows.anchor: فالربيبة محرمة سواء كانت في حجر زوج أمها أو لم تكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The household phrase may point to the rationale for prohibiting close relations: regular domestic mixing makes avoiding immorality difficult if only adultery itself is forbidden.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما يستفاد من حكمة تشريع الحرمة في محرمات النسب والسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stepdaughter's residence is not a legal condition: the text explicitly makes consummation a condition, and would likewise have stated residence if that mattered.
rows.anchor: ولو كان الكون في الحجور مثله لكان من اللازم ذكره وهو ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'No blame upon you' means no blame in marrying the stepdaughters; the verb is omitted for concision because context supplies it.
rows.anchor: أي في أن تنكحوهن حذف إيثارا للاختصار لدلالة السياق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines ḥalāʾil as wives made lawful to each other, deriving the word from ḥalāl; it also reports an alternative derivation from cohabiting in the same bed.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع والحلائل جمع الحليلة وهي بمعنى محللة مشتقة من الحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sons include descendants connected by birth directly or through a son or daughter; 'from your loins' excludes a son's wife when the son is adopted rather than biological.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأبناء من اتصل بالإنسان بولادة سواء كان ذلك بلا واسطة أو بواسطة ابن أو بنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on combining two sisters means simultaneous marriage while the first wife remains married; after her death or divorce, marrying her sister is permitted, as continuous Muslim practice shows.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق الكلام ينصرف إلى الجمع بينهما في النكاح في زمان واحد فلا مانع من أن ينكح الرجل إحدى الأختين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for past conduct pardons pre-Islamic Arab marriages combining sisters, rather than permitting a preexisting combination to continue after revelation; the text's treatment of fathers' wives supports this reading.
rows.anchor: ناظر إلى ما كان معمولا به بين عرب الجاهلية من الجمع بين الأختين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although pardoning a completed past act has no direct practical effect, it matters for consequences that remain, including legitimate birth and recognition of kinship after children are born.
rows.anchor: لكنه لا يخلو عن الفائدة من حيث آثار العمل الباقية بعده كطهارة المولد واعتبار القرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says an interlocutor confuses a rational purpose for a law with the law's textual scope, wrongly making legal permission expand or contract with the purpose.
rows.anchor: خلط البحث في ملاك الحكم المسمى بحكمة التشريع بالبحث عن نفس الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational inquiry identifies a law's rationale, while the legal ruling, its subject, and its conditions follow the lawgiver's verbal statement.
rows.anchor: وأحد البحثين وهو البحث عن الملاك عقلي والآخر وهو البحث عن الحكم الشرعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All enacted rulings rest on real interests; marriage's predominant purpose is procreation and reproduction, contributing to the human species' continued existence.
rows.anchor: وإنا لا نشك أن جميع الأحكام المشرعة تتبع مصالح وملاكات حقيقية وحكم النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nature equips humans with reproductive organs and sexual desire to draw the sexes together, while reason helps prevent corruption of this divinely intended path.
rows.anchor: بتجهيز البنية الإنسانية بجهاز التناسل الذي يفصل أجزاء منه فيربيه ويكونه إنسانا جديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproductive rationale is only general: not every union, sexual act, desire, or person leads to a child, and attraction does not compel every couple toward conception.
rows.anchor: فليس كل ازدواج مؤديا إلى ظهور الولد ولا كل عمل تناسلي كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marriage legislation also protects people from sexual immorality, which damages domestic happiness, destroys households, and interrupts lineage; together with procreation this is its predominant rationale.
rows.anchor: مصلحة الاستيلاد والأمن من دبيب الفحشاء هي الملاك الغالبي الذي بني عليه تشريع النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because legal rules remain permanent even when their predominant rationale is absent, marriage or intercourse need not be intended to produce children or form a household; infertility, age, youth, pregnancy, or lack of ejaculation does not itself negate permission.
rows.anchor: فليس من الجائز أن يقال إن النكاح أو المباشرة يتبعان في جوازهما الغرض والملاك المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the temporary-marriage ruling was abrogated by the Qur'an or Sunna; reports variously place the Prophet's prohibition at Khaybar, the conquest, or the Farewell Pilgrimage, and say permission and prohibition recurred before prohibition settled.
rows.anchor: الآية، وقيل منسوخة بالسنة نسخها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عام خيبر وقيل عام الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the Meccan passage in al-Muʾminūn abrogated the Medinan temporary-marriage verse fails because a Meccan verse cannot abrogate a later Medinan one.
rows.anchor: فإنها مكية وآية المتعة مدنية ولا تصلح المكية لنسخ المدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Temporary marriage is a marriage and the woman is a wife, as prophetic reports and early Muslim authorities call it; objections based on inheritance or divorce are answered later.
rows.anchor: ممنوع وناهيك في ذلك ما وقع في الأخبار النبوية وفي كلمات السلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance, divorce, and waiting-period passages relate to temporary marriage as general or unrestricted texts qualified by Sunna, which excludes some spouses; they do not abrogate the temporary-marriage verse.
rows.anchor: ففيه أن النسبة بينها وبين آية المتعة ليست نسبة الناسخ والمنسوخ بل نسبة العام والمخصص أو المطلق والمقيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some legal theorists hold that a general text following a specific one abrogates it, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects that rule here because the temporary-marriage verse came after the general passages.
rows.anchor: نعم ذهب بعض الأصوليين فيما إذا ورد خاص ثم عقبه عام يخالفه في الإثبات والنفي إلى أن العام ناسخ للخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting-period rule also applies to temporary marriage, with a different duration, so it qualifies rather than abrogates the ruling.
rows.anchor: فإن حكم العدة جار في المنقطعة كالدائمة وإن اختلفتا مدة فيؤول إلى التخصيص أيضا دون النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited-women passage and its allowance of other women by marriage or ownership form one continuous statement; because temporary marriage is marriage, there is no contradiction or abrogation.
rows.anchor: فلأن الآية غير صريحة ولا ظاهرة في النهي عن الزوجية غير الدائمة بوجه من الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated aim of easing religious burdens connects with the prayer against burdens imposed on earlier communities and the declaration that religion contains no hardship; it displays the fullness of God's human blessings in this community.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن النكتة في هذا التعليل العام بيان ظهور تمام النعم الإنسانية في هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says nursing prohibits the same relations as lineage.
rows.anchor: إن الله حرم من الرضاعة ما حرم من النسب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet also describes milk kinship as being like kinship by lineage.
rows.anchor: الرضاع لحمة كلحمة النسب

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that ten known nursing sessions were revealed, then abrogated by five, which remained recited at the Prophet's death; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this as an alteration report that conflicts with the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت كان فيما أنزل من القرآن عشر رضعات معلومات فنسخن بخمس معلومات

rows.speaker: النبي عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a man may not marry his wife's mother whether or not he consummated the marriage, but may marry her daughter after divorcing the mother without consummation.
rows.anchor:
عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال
" إذا نكح الرجل المرأة فلا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this rule is also transmitted through the Shia Imams and follows the verse's meaning; he rejects Sunni reports allowing the wife's mother before consummation or exempting stepdaughters outside the home.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى مروي من طرق الشيعة عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام وهو مذهبهم وهو المستفاد من الكتاب

rows.speaker: الصادق عن منصور بن حازم
rows.claim: In a report about marrying the mother of a wife who died before consummation, al-Ṣādiq cites ʿAlī's distinction: the stepdaughter's prohibition is conditional on consummation, while the wife's mother is unqualified.
rows.anchor: فقال علي عليه السلام إن هذه مستثناة وهذه مرسلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recounts regretting that he challenged al-Ṣādiq's account by asserting that ʿAlī had ruled otherwise; the Imam rebukes him for citing that report and then asking for his own ruling.
rows.anchor: فلما قمت ندمت وقلت أي شيء صنعت؟ يقول قد فعله رجل منا ولم ير به بأسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in al-Durr al-manthūr says a man who married without consummation was first allowed by Ibn Masʿūd to marry his wife's mother, then ordered to separate after Ibn Masʿūd learned the ruling in Medina.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا من بني شمخ تزوج امرأة ولم يدخل بها ثم رأى أمها فأعجبته فاستفتى ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes that this story is not attributed to ʿAlī in that source; it is attributed to the Prophet's Companions, with another version naming ʿUmar, and reports place the condition on stepdaughters.
rows.anchor: لكن لم ينسب القول فيه إلى علي عليه السلام بل ذكر أنه سأل عنه أصحاب النبي

rows.speaker: علي عن إسحاق بن عمار عن جعفر عن أبيه
rows.claim: A report attributed to ʿAlī says stepdaughters are forbidden after consummation whether they live in the home or elsewhere, while mothers-in-law are unconditionally forbidden.
rows.anchor: أن عليا عليه السلام كان يقول الربائب عليكم حرام مع الأمهات اللاتي دخلتم بهن في الحجور وغير الحجور سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some Sunni reports ascribe a home-residence condition to ʿAlī, the Imams' reports reject it and agree with the verse's apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: لكن الروايات المأثورة عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام تدفعه وهو الموافق لما يستفاد من الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubhamāt means unqualified or undifferentiated; it refers to prohibited classes whose ban has no condition, including mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts, nieces, milk relations, mothers-in-law, and sons' wives.
rows.anchor: والمبهمات من البهمة وهي كون الشيء ذا لون واحد لا يختلط به لون آخر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عن زرارة
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir says a man who has intercourse with his enslaved woman may not marry her daughter, invoking the verse's rule for stepdaughters.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سألته عن الرجل تكون له الجارية فيصيب منها أله أن ينكح ابنتها

rows.speaker: علي عن أبي صالح الحنفي عن أبي عون
rows.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwā asks about a milk sister and two enslaved sisters, ʿAlī calls the question futile and says the two sisters are allowed by one verse and prohibited by another; he neither rules nor practices it.
rows.anchor: قال علي عليه السلام ذات يوم سلوني فقال ابن الكوا أخبرني عن بنت الأخت من الرضاعة وعن المملوكتين الأختين

rows.speaker: الصادق عن معمر بن يحيى بن سالم
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq explains that ʿAlī knew two verses addressed the enslaved-sister issue; when asked whether one abrogated the other or both remained operative, he says ʿAlī feared people would disobey, and would have implemented the whole Qur'an if firmly obeyed.
rows.anchor: قد أحلتها آية وحرمتها آية أخرى فقلنا الأول أن يكون إحداهما نسخت الأخرى أم هما محكمتان
